rationale: Both candidates correctly validate that the ground-truth blockers (partition-specific enabler, offline example variable) are already fixed in this diff, and both independently rediscover the two concerns that remain live: the engine-level 0.2 default silently overriding the new MiniMax-H3 0.17 default, and the e2e smoke test's failure to assert an actual cache hit — matching the human reviewer's own caveat almost verbatim. Y edges out on precision and actionability: its critical finding is backed by an execution trace, its suggested fixes are more directly prescriptive (exact line to delete, exact code to move), and it surfaces one finding (the 39→107 frame change silently altering the unrelated FP8 smoke test) that is directly verifiable in the visible diff. X's extra findings are bulkier but include weaker, more speculative items (a major claim about the untouched quality_policy.py file, a CI-gate question, a title nit) that add fabrication/relevance risk without matching grounding strength.
